title.rendered: Captain crashes the Costa Concordia and leaves 32 dead. Then, he’s released from prison after 9 years: ‘I tripped and I ended up in one of the boats’

content.rendered:
Francesco Schettino, captain of the Costa Concordia cruise ship when it sank in 2012, has been released from prison after serving nine and a half years of his 16-year prison sentence, according to Italian newspaper Quotidiano Nazionale, as reported by the New York Post. His release follows a court finding that he completed a rehabilitation and behavior program.

In 2012, the Costa Concordia ran aground near Giglio, a Tuscan island. The damage to the hull caused the ship to capsize. In all, 32 passengers died, and Schettino was convicted of manslaughter for those deaths, as well as causing a maritime disaster and abandoning ship.

Autopsies of the victims showed that the majority of them drowned either on the ship or from falling into the sea during the chaos. Schettino escaped on a lifeboat and refused orders to return to the ship. To explain how he ended up on a lifeboat, he said, “suddenly, since the ship was at a 60- to 70-degree angle, I tripped, and I ended up in one of the boats,” which led to news outlets giving him the nickname “Captain Coward.”

Captains are legally obligated to assist every passenger to get off the ship

NPR spoke with Rod Sullivan, then a professor of maritime law at the Florida Coastal School of Law in Jacksonville, Florida, about this case in 2012. Steve Inskeep led the interview and asked, “What actually is the captain’s responsibility under maritime law?”

According to Sullivan, the old saying that the captain has to go down with the ship isn’t exactly what maritime law says. Instead, he explained that “in the modern Merchant Marine and in connection with passenger ships, he is legally required to render assistance to every single person trying to get off that ship, and also identify those people who may have been killed in the incident.”

Inskeep also asked if Sullivan believed that Schettino should face criminal charges for the incident regarding the Costa Concordia, as this interview took place before he was sentenced in 2015. Sullivan said, “In my opinion, this captain was grossly negligent and reckless, both in causing the collision and in the inappropriate abandon-ship procedures, and then leaving the ship. So, yes, I think he should be subject to criminal charges.”

Schettino’s remaining sentence will reportedly be probation

According to the outlet, Schettino’s remaining seven years will be served as supervised probation. La Repubblica reports that there are terms to his probation, and that his sentence still stands during this period. The outlet claims that if Schettino violates his probation terms, he could be returned to prison.

For a more detailed look at what happened to this ship, Netflix released a documentary, Shipwrecked: Nightmare at Sea, in June 2026 that covered the Costa Concordia’s story and spoke to survivors of the incident.

title.rendered: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping rushes through the moments that made the book hurt

content.rendered:
Spoilers for the book and movie follow.

The tissues stayed in my bag through all of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping. After sobbing through Suzanne Collins’ book and doing it all over again with the audiobook, bringing them felt like common sense. The sadness came later that night, at home, when I realized how much of Haymitch’s story I’d wanted to spend more time with.

Joseph Zada is fantastic as Haymitch, and Kelvin Harrison Jr. sounds and moves so much like the younger Beetee I’d pictured that it’s a little eerie. After all those fancasts, it was cool to see who ended up playing everyone and to finally see the arena. I just wish the movie had spent as much time on Haymitch and the other tributes as it did bringing their world to life.

Directed by Francis Lawrence, Sunrise on the Reaping follows a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy after he’s reaped for the Second Quarter Quell, a special edition of the Games with twice as many tributes. It’s a faithful adaptation that builds the world of Panem beautifully and gets the casting right. Where it stumbles is in how quickly it moves past the people at the center of the story.

Haymitch’s applause needed a little more time

Louella McCoy is one of the kids sent to the Hunger Games from District 12 alongside Haymitch for the Second Quarter Quell. She dies before the Games even start, when her chariot crashes during a parade introducing the tributes. Haymitch looks up at President Snow and starts clapping. Even knowing why he did it, my first thought was, Wait, we’re there already?

In the book, Haymitch brings Louella beneath Snow’s balcony, hoping the cameras are still rolling. He wants everyone watching to see him give the president a round of applause for getting a child killed at his own parade.

If you’re seeing the story for the first time, you’re still taking in Louella’s death when Haymitch starts clapping. A second to see him decide what he’s about to do would’ve helped. He’s publicly blaming the president for Louella’s death before he’s even made it into the arena. Snow still gets to decide what happens to him.

Haymitch and Maysilee needed more time together

Haymitch covering Maysilee with his poncho as she dies broke my heart. It also made me miss a cup, of all things. The movie keeps the part where Maysilee shows off the utensils she made herself after demanding silverware from the Capitol. In the book, she pulls them out right after Haymitch teases her about having to eat without silverware. She makes him laugh, and he offers her a cup he got from a sponsor to complete the set. He’s trying to earn her trust, and there’s something so sweet about him doing it by playing along with her.

By the time they say they think of each other as brother and sister, they’ve already had a moment where they sound like siblings giving each other a hard time over dinner. The Games give them so little say in what happens to them, and they still get to decide they’re family. I wanted a little more of that in the movie before I had to watch Haymitch lose his sister.

So, when are we getting that Plutarch book?

Knowing Plutarch eventually helps overthrow Snow makes it so much fun to watch him be polite to the man. How long has he been sitting across from Snow, smiling and agreeing with him? How much of it does Snow actually buy? Suzanne Collins, if you ever want to spend a whole book on those two, please do.

Part of me envies the people on TikTok who saved the book until after the movie. Knowing what was coming hadn’t stopped me from crying through the audiobook, so I figured the movie would get me all over again. Instead, I was still taking in what had happened to one tribute when the movie moved on to the next. I wish it had stayed with them a little longer.

title.rendered: Mamdani releases 84,000 more records on Sept. 11 attacks after city portal gets 11 million visits: ‘Our work is not finished’

content.rendered:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has released another 84,000 records related to the September 11, 2001, attacks. This update brings the total number of pages available in the city public portal to more than 440,000. According to The Hill, the release marks the third installment of documents made public following a legal agreement between the city and 9/11 Health Watch. 

The online archive, launched in September around the 25th anniversary of the attacks, has surpassed 11 million unique visits. Mayor Mamdani emphasized that his administration is committed to full transparency regarding the government response to the terror attacks. In a press release issued Sunday, November 22, 2026, he stated, “After the horrific terror attacks of September 11th and the devastating health consequences that followed, New Yorkers across the five boroughs demanded transparency from their government – but were met with silence.” 

He noted, “We launched the City’s first public portal to make these records accessible to the people who have waited decades for answers.” While the portal has already seen massive engagement, the mayor made it clear that the project is not finished. He stated, “More than 11 million visits and 440,000 pages later, our work is not finished. We will continue releasing records until survivors, first responders and families have the information and clarity they deserve.”

The documents provide a look at the city response in the aftermath of the attacks

This is specifically regarding air quality, debris, and potential toxins in Lower Manhattan. These materials have been a focal point for advocates like Benjamin Chevat, the executive director of 9/11 Health Watch. Chevat has previously expressed that the files show “a disturbing record” from city, state, and federal officials. He alleged that these officials did not properly address hazards, noting they may have been “slowing down a return to homes, schools and offices, or by better cleanup efforts in those places.”

Beyond the historical significance, these records serve a very practical purpose for those still struggling with health issues today. First responders and survivors are actively searching the archive for proof of their presence at or near Ground Zero. Newsweek reports that this documentation can be vital for those applying to the World Trade Center Health Program or the September 11th Victim Compensation Fund. 

Eligibility for these federal programs often depends on where an individual was, what they were doing, and how long they spent at specific sites. While the city archive does not guarantee that a specific document will satisfy every federal requirement, it provides a new resource for those trying to build their cases. Chevat noted that his group has already identified two individuals whose cases could be supported by documents found in the archive.

The effort to organize and publish these files is being led by the New York City Law Department

New York City Corporation Counsel Steven Banks described the project as a way to dismantle “decades of municipal bureaucracy and delay.” He stated that this release marks “another step toward fulfilling the City’s commitment to providing New Yorkers with an unvarnished window into the City’s post-9/11 response.”

The release also addresses a long-standing question about what city officials knew regarding the toxic air conditions. Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal highlighted this. “Every new release helps answer a question that first responders, survivors and their families have asked for 25 years: When did City Hall learn that the air at Ground Zero could make people sick?” he said. He thanked the mayor and the corporation counsel for their roles in bringing these records to light.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin also weighed in on the importance of the ongoing project. She pointed out that the tragedy of September 11 did not end on the day of the attacks and noted that tens of thousands of New Yorkers have suffered from serious illnesses linked to the conditions in Lower Manhattan. “While nothing can undo that suffering or bring back those we have lost, we owe survivors, first responders, and their families the truth about the dangers they faced,” she said.

The administration has allocated $34 million in the fiscal 2027 budget to create and maintain the portal. This ensures that the public will have continued access to the material as more batches are released. The city confirmed that additional records will be made available in the coming months. Those looking to access the documents can visit the portal at nyc.gov/sept11docs.

title.rendered: Hakeem Jeffries gears up to work with the Trump administration. Then he names the one man he refuses to sit across from: ‘A stone-cold racist’

content.rendered:
Hakeem Jeffries is preparing to lead the House as speaker, but he is drawing a firm line when it comes to the White House staff. According to Fox News, the New York Democrat made it clear that he refuses to meet with White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller. During an interview with The New York Times, Jeffries did not hold back his feelings about the appointment. He labeled Miller as a “stone-cold racist” and explained why he intends to avoid any direct negotiations with him.

This decision creates a unique dynamic as the new administration begins its work in January. Jeffries insisted in the interview on Saturday, November 21, 2026, that this is not a boycott of the administration itself. He said he remains open to finding ways to move legislation forward for the American people but simply believes that Miller is not a person he can engage with in good faith. “I’ve made it clear that Stephen Miller is a stone-cold racist. Why would I deal with him at this point in time?” Jeffries said. 

He pointed to his long history of criticizing Miller, particularly regarding immigration policies. Jeffries described Miller as the “architect of Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine.” He claimed that the policies associated with this agenda have led to chaos, cruelty, and death. He specifically referenced the deaths of Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good during enforcement actions as evidence of the harm he believes these policies cause.

The White House has pushed back against these characterizations

White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers defended Miller’s record in a statement. She argued, “Unlike the hardcore, partisan Democrats who refused to work with the President and blocked many of his popular policies, Stephen Miller has a track record of spearheading bipartisan efforts: public safety reform, making our cities such as Washington, D.C., and Memphis safe again, drug pricing transparency, and unleashing a nuclear energy renaissance.”

President Trump also weighed in on the situation during an appearance on Saturday in America with Kayleigh McEnany. He defended his choice of Chief of Staff while also offering some surprising words for Jeffries. Trump acknowledged the label Jeffries used but stood by his aide. “So, he called him a racist. But we had to be strong,” Trump said. He added that Miller was very strong on the border, which he considers a priority.

Interestingly, Trump also spoke highly of the incoming speaker. He called Jeffries a “very smart” and “reasonable guy.” 

The president noted the significance of Jeffries becoming the first Black person to hold the speakership, per The Hill. “I give him a lot of congratulations. What he did was pretty spectacular, with getting that position. And it’s nice: first Black person in that position – it’s a big deal. It’s a big deal, and he should be very proud of himself,” Trump stated. He also mentioned that he looks forward to working with the Democratic leader in the next Congress.

Jeffries is mapping out how he intends to handle White House communications

The Speaker-designate told The New York Times that he does not need to go through the Chief of Staff to get things done. He plans to reach out to the president directly or work through Vice President J.D. Vance. Jeffries noted that the president is not a hard person to reach. He also mentioned that congressional leaders often work through Cabinet secretaries or the vice president to manage legislative business.

Jeffries noted that he has already spoken with Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. However, when pressed, he clarified that he does not necessarily like any of the Cabinet secretaries at this point in time. He is focused on keeping an open line of communication to ensure that the House can function effectively. Jeffries emphasized that his goal is to maintain a willingness to work with politicians across the aisle.

Trump also expressed a desire to work in a bipartisan way to avoid legislative gridlock. He pointed out that he holds significant power in the process. “Look, I have the power,” Trump said during his interview. He explained that he could choose to veto everything for his entire term, but he prefers to find common ground. “There’s a chance we could get great healthcare and a lot of other things, and we do it in a bipartisan way,” Trump noted. He warned that if they cannot agree, nothing will get done for anyone.

The president also mentioned that he knows Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer well. He believes there is a chance for the government to do historic work. Trump mentioned that they will each bring their own points of view to the table. He believes that if they handle things correctly, they might even be able to touch the subject of immigration.

Russell Brand’s wife films new Sunday Service episode, vows to ‘absolutely honor’ rules after his prison message explodes online amid outcry

content.rendered:
Laura Brand is moving forward with her online content while promising to follow strict prison guidelines. According to The Guardian, in a new episode of the Brands’ Sunday Service YouTube series on Sunday, November 22, 2026, she explained her intent to respect the parameters set by the staff at HMP Littlehey. This announcement comes after a recent video featuring a message from her husband, Russell Brand, caused a major public reaction.

The comedian is currently serving a ten-and-a-half-year sentence after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault at Southwark crown court on November 5, 2026. Following that sentencing, Laura Brand read a statement from her husband in a video titled ‘The Good Work Continues.’ In that message, the actor insisted he was not guilty of the charges. This specific video remains on YouTube, despite requests from government officials for the platform to remove it.

The video has gained over 1 million views, making it the most popular upload on Brand’s channel. Before this surge, the channel had largely seen lower engagement, with many videos attracting between 50,000 and 100,000 views. The last time the channel saw similar numbers was in December of last year during a conversation with political commentator Candace Owens.

‘Why are we having to hear from him?’

U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham recently commented on the situation. While he noted that he would not jump to changing laws to force social media companies to take down such content, he did call for them to act. He stated, “I would call on those social media companies to take these interviews down. You know, why are we having to hear from him? We shouldn’t be, and certainly [the victims] shouldn’t be hearing from him.”

Laura Brand addressed the ongoing situation during her latest broadcast. She told her audience, “Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention and now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant and professional staff at HMP Littlehey, I will absolutely honour that.” She appears to be navigating a complex situation as she continues to manage the digital presence of her husband while he remains incarcerated.

The Ministry of Justice has been looking into whether the released message violated rules designed to prevent serious distress to victims of crime. According to Page Six, Burnham’s office stated, “Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.” 

Despite the controversy, Laura Brand remains committed to the project

Laura said she is choosing to continue Sunday Service because she really enjoys the series. She said, “It is also a place where I will continue to be proud to be a wife, a mother and a woman defending her family at a time when the media’s image of what kind of a woman I am is under so much scrutiny.” Laura has been a constant presence by Russell’s side throughout the legal proceedings.

The couple, who have been married since August 2017, share three children. During the legal process, she reportedly told him that she loved him and would be okay after the sentencing was handed down. According to Us Weekly, in the new video, she said, “We trust God, and we trust his plan, and we trust everything He’s doing right now, even though it’s painful. Obviously, [it] will take some getting used to for me to even sit here and not have my companion and my person with me.”

Meanwhile, other aspects of the comedian’s brand have continued to operate

His wellness shop has launched merchandise featuring the phrase ‘Free Russell Brand’. The website invites visitors to stand with him against what it describes as injustice. These items, including T-shirts and a baseball cap, are being sold for $34.99. The site features a button that leads users to the shop, and claims that he has been silenced from speaking out.

The legal journey for the 51-year-old actor has been extensive. He faced accusations in 2023 and maintained his innocence throughout the trial, pleading not guilty to multiple counts of rape and sexual assault. While he was acquitted of some charges, the conviction on the remaining counts led to his current prison term.
